title: Write a feature-task PR body's Acceptance Criteria section
description: The model is asked to write the `## Acceptance Criteria` section of a feature-task PR body from a task description and the pr-open evidence rules. The grader is the production lobster parser (`feature-task ac-check`), so the score is whether the real gate would accept the body — not whether a reimplementation of the parser thinks so.
why_it_matters: This is the failure class that has actually cost us tasks: a PR body whose AC text or evidence annotation the lobster will not accept, so the task bounces back to `doing` at the acceptance gate. It is a clean pass/fail with a known right answer, which makes it the highest-signal eval in the set.
prompt:
You are writing the `## Acceptance Criteria` section of a feature-task pull request body.

Three input files, all reproduced in full below:
- `task-description.md` — the feature task description. Its `## Acceptance Criteria` block lists the task's ACs.
- `pr-open-excerpt.md` — the evidence-annotation rules a PR author must follow, and the list of files changed in this PR.
- `pr-files.txt` — the changed-file list, repeated separately so its exact contents are unambiguous.

Using those, produce the PR body's `## Acceptance Criteria` section for that task, exactly as a careful PR author would write it under those rules:
- every task AC appears, as a `- [x]` line, with the AC label and the AC sentence copied verbatim from the task description
- each line ends with exactly one recognised evidence annotation

Output only the `## Acceptance Criteria` section: the heading and the AC lines. No commentary, no code fence, no trailing prose.
